_comment_family: Futura Bold, leaned and tightened for one channel: CANAL+. The
show's guidelines name a house face, 'Canalp', set bold, italic and
at a letter spacing of -50; the show supplied Futura Bold as the face
to stand in for it. The file it supplied is upright and has no
italic, and the renderer has neither an italic of its own nor a
letter-spacing control - so both are baked into THIS file instead,
and the renderer sees an ordinary face whose outlines and advances
already are what the guidelines ask for.
Baked rather than taught to text.js on purpose. Every measurement
the layout takes - the width fit, the ink bounds, the cap band a box
is padded from - is read off the font through Fabric and through a
plain canvas context side by side, and a slant or a spacing applied
at the draw would have to be applied identically on both paths or
the boxes would be measured against letters nobody draws. In the
file, both paths read the same outlines and cannot disagree.
How it was made, from the supplied 'Futura Bold.otf' (CFF outlines,
1000 units to the em, cap height 754), with fontTools:
- every outline skewed 12 degrees to the right, about half the
cap height (x' = x + tan(12) * (y - 377)), so a capital leans
round its own middle instead of sliding right as a whole. 12 is
what the stems in the guidelines' own screenshots measure;
- every advance reduced by 50 units, which is exactly what a
letter spacing of -50 means in the editor the guidelines were
written in (thousandths of an em, applied after every glyph,
the space included). The GPOS kerning pairs are untouched and
still apply on top of it;
- the left side bearings recomputed from the skewed outlines, the
italic angle set to -12, and the style bits set to bold italic;
- renamed throughout (see below).
The family is 'Futura Bold Oblique CANAL' in every name record and
the PostScript name 'FuturaBold-ObliqueCANAL'. A name of its own is
the point: a machine with a real Futura installed answers to
'Futura', and `registerFace` in js/channels.js skips a family that is
already present - so under the original name the channel would be
drawn in the machine's upright Futura, at its full spacing, and
fontguard would pass it because the family did arrive.
The Latin accents a French or Portuguese caption needs are all in
the file.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css. This face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON at load time (see registerFace in
js/channels.js), which is the route content/README.md describes.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file
and used by the installer as the name it registers this face under
(see engine.install_fonts, which takes the first). The PostScript
name first, then the full name. 'Futura' and 'Futura Bold' are
deliberately absent: they name the upright, untracked original, and
a machine answering to either would hand back the wrong letters.
_comment_stack: Damage limitation, never a design choice - a block laid out against
the wrong metrics is broken rather than merely different, which is
what fontguard exists to catch before anything is drawn.
Geometric sans faces in falling order of likeness: the original
Futura where a machine has it (upright and loose, but the right
skeleton), then Century Gothic, which ships with Office on most of
the machines this runs on, then the floor.
stack: 'Futura Bold Oblique CANAL', 'Futura', 'Century Gothic', Arial, sans-serif
